title: In 590 imaged zebrafish integrator cells, higher eye-position sensitivity came with less persistence; the hindbrain connectome model and 400 rewired models gave the opposite sign
abstract: Question: does the published linear model of the larval zebrafish hindbrain eye-position integrator, built from EM synapse counts (Vishwanathan et al. 2024), give the measured relation between the eye-position sensitivity K of a cell and the persistence of its post-saccadic activity, and the measured spatial maps of both? Approach: we used the published model data and imaging table, put EM somata and imaged cells in the shared frame, and compared the real wiring with 200 degree-preserving shuffles, 200 distance-preserving rewirings and position permutations. Results: in 590 imaged integrator cells pooled from about 20 larvae, cells with higher K were less persistent (Spearman -0.27, cell bootstrap 95% CI -0.35 to -0.19; same sign for four persistence measures, high-SNR cells, after position control and on each side). The connectome model gave +0.80, all model variants +0.79 to +0.94, and all 400 null wirings gave positive values (+0.32 to +0.80). Thus the conflict comes from the model class, in which one slow mode sets both K and persistence. The real wiring gave a wider persistence spread across cells (IQR/median 0.56) than all 400 null wirings (0.11 to 0.41), because a second mode stays near the leading one (|lambda2|/lambda1 0.77). Model maps mapped onto 265 nearby imaged cells did not predict measured persistence beyond a position-permutation null (r +0.20, p 0.125) and gave the wrong sign for K (r -0.20). Limitations: larva identity is not in the table, so CIs are too narrow; EM and imaging come from different larvae; we did not test mechanisms such as burst input or intrinsic leak that could reverse the sign. External data are not bundled; a fetch script and hashes are included.

display.caption: Sensitivity-persistence coupling. (a) 590 imaged VPNI cells and ABD motoneurons: higher K, less persistence (Spearman -0.27). (b) Connectome model, EM integrator cells: +0.80. (c) Coupling for data (with 95% cell bootstrap CI), model variants and 400 null wirings; all models are positive.

Real wiring gives a wider spread of model persistence across cells (a) and a second mode nearer the leading one (b) than 200 degree-preserving shuffles and 200 distance-preserving rewirings. Orange lines: potential-synapse connectomes from the source study.

Spatial maps. (a) Measured persistence of imaged cells (mirrored to one side). (b) Model persistence of EM integrator cells. (c) Spearman r between model maps (kNN mapped) and 265 nearby imaged cells for real wiring (green), against position permutation and wiring nulls (boxes, 2.5-97.5% whiskers) and the data self-prediction ceiling (dashed).
